summary: Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar. Kawasaki served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

Esho Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Sasaki held posts as an associate professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Esho Yamaguchi is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1942. Yamaguchi held positions at Ritsumeikan University and served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 1980–1984).

Eshō Mikogami (1935–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū. He was president of the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies in 1997, a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003, and later professor emeritus.

Ester Bianchi is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD studying under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE (~1999–2003), later teaching at the University of Perugia (~2007).

Etsuaki Teraishi is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Teraishi served as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a special research fellow for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler (~1880–1886). From circa 1886 to 1903, he served as an epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India, Government of Madras, and Government of India.

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1873–1876) and served at Tongwen Guan in 1881 as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German.

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under August Schleicher (~1860–1864) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1909. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1908–1913), Johns Hopkins University (~1913–1917), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield (~1990–1997), taught at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997), and became Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor at Harvard University (~1997).

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a Polish scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lviv University (~1919–1924) and held posts at Lviv University (~1934–1939), Nicolaus Copernicus University (~1945–1969), and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852) was a French Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1822–1832). He served as secretary of the Société Asiatique (1826, 1832) and taught at the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Obermiller (1901–1935) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1935). He held positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1930–1935).

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. She was an assistant professor at the University of Michigan until 2004, when she joined Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from Korea University. Choi held an HK professor post at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2015).

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She served as Professor Emeritus and Department Chair of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary (both attested 2006).
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held an academic post at the University of Calgary.

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied under Robert A. F. Thurman at Amherst and Francisco Varela at Toronto. He held posts at Concordia, York, the University of Toronto (2005), and the University of British Columbia (2013).
